擦 concerns rubbing, scraping or scrubbing a surface. [摩擦](../words/摩擦.md) まさつ is friction or rubbing, and [擦る](../words/擦る.md) こする is an everyday verb, "rub; scrub; scrape," though it is usually written in kana. The same character writes 擦り傷 すりきず, "scratch; graze; scrape; abrasion," and the formal term 擦過傷 さっかしょう, "abrasion; scratch; graze," where the scraping leaves a mark on the skin. The word かする, "to graze," can also be written 擦る, but かす.る is not a KANJIDIC2 reading and is not part of the metadata here.

**Modern-shape mnemonic, not etymology:** find 扌, the side form of [手](手.md), "hand," at the left and [察](察.md), "observe; infer," at the right. Imagine a hand rubbing a surface; the right-hand part 察 also reads サツ, which makes a handy sound cue. This is a memory aid only: it makes no claim about the historical formation of 擦.

## Meaning and origin

削 concerns shaving or cutting material away. [削る](../words/削る.md) けずる can mean sharpening a pencil by shaving it, reducing an amount, or deleting part of a text. In [削除](../words/削除.md) さくじょ, the focus is deletion or erasure, not necessarily a physical cut.

## Common words

- [削る](../words/削る.md) けずる — shave; sharpen; cut down
- [削除](../words/削除.md) さくじょ — deletion; erasure
- 削減 さくげん — reduction; cut
- 添削 てんさく — correction of writing

Two practical uses of けずる are 鉛筆を削る (えんぴつをけずる), "sharpen a pencil," and 予算を削る (よさんをけずる), "cut the budget."
